startup.name: Paradev (formerly Superset)
startup.description: Open-source desktop IDE that runs hundreds of coding agents in parallel, with tens of thousands of engineers using it and plans for a collaborative cross-platform tool. Four person team; developers and engineering teams would pay.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already accepted, so this is a note. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. Real open source usage in the tens of thousands, a technical team and a hot category would lift odds sharply, while a crowded category of parallel agent tools lowers them.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because parallel agent IDEs are crowded, with Conductor, Cursor and others offering the same worktree workflow, and open source usage does not show willingness to pay. A reviewer may see a feature that the model labs will absorb into their own coding apps.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C fails because companies in this category are often acquired early, as Continue was in the data, so independence to C is rare. Model labs and IDE vendors are the natural buyers, and a large lab shipping the same product removes the market.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The common failure is commoditization: model providers and large IDEs ship parallel agent features for free, and open source forks reproduce the interface. The company then either sells early for its team and users or fades when the community moves on. Most analogs in the cohort that did not reach a later round also lacked a repeatable paying customer base, and exits in this category tend to be small.

killers.risk: Model labs and IDE vendors bundle parallel agents
killers.evidence: Cursor already runs parallel agents in worktrees and other IDEs added the feature in 2026, leaving little room for a standalone product.
killers.mitigation: Stay agent agnostic and own team collaboration and review workflows.

killers.risk: Open source usage never converts to revenue
killers.evidence: Free individual usage with users paying for their own model subscriptions gives limited pricing power, as with Vibe Kanban.
killers.mitigation: Launch team plans with shared cloud workspaces and track conversion.

killers.risk: Fast follower competition from many similar tools
killers.evidence: The comps show a dozen similar parallel agent tools in 2024 to 2026 batches.
killers.mitigation: Move to cross platform and cloud collaboration before rivals.

killers.risk: Distraction from a rename and pivot to self-improving software
killers.evidence: The new tagline is broader than the product with traction, which can dilute focus.
killers.mitigation: Ship the core product improvements first.

technical_complexity.rationale: Worktree management, agent adapters and a desktop app are buildable by a small team in months, so complexity is moderate. The hard part is cross platform collaboration and keeping up with changing agent interfaces.

takeover_risk.rationale: Model labs and IDEs ship similar features within months and already distribute to the same developers, and several have added parallel agent features, so copy risk is extremely high.

evidence.claim: Many engineers run several coding agents at once, and a set of paid tools has appeared to manage them.
Review burden and the need for orchestration are recurring complaints, which supports demand for a control layer.

brand.name: Paradev
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Paradev" --era 2022+ : kind invented_or_proper, alive 92.7 percent, n=1826
weaknesses: Rename from Superset can lose search and community equity
brand.rationale: Paradev is a short invented name that hints at parallel development, which fits the product. A rename risks lost recognition after the open source community knew it as Superset, but the effect on outcomes is small compared with distribution.

narrative.headline: Strong early usage in a crowded, fast moving category, so a seed is likely but independence to later rounds is uncertain.
narrative.general_summary: Paradev is an open source desktop IDE that lets engineers run many coding agents in parallel, and it claims tens of thousands of users. In 2026 that is the kind of traction that attracts seed money, so a round above the YC check within a year is likely. The risk is structural: Cursor, Zed and the model labs ship parallel agents themselves, there are a dozen similar YC companies, and free usage does not prove revenue. Analogs split between an early acquisition and shutdowns. A pivot to team collaboration and cloud workspaces is the upside path. About 35 percent of simulated paths end in a stall.
